mainEntity.name: How long does primary closure take to heal after implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: The initial soft tissue healing of a primarily closed wound typically takes around 7–14 days. During this period, the gum tissue knits together and sutures either dissolve or are removed. However, the deeper healing process — including osseointegration of the implant with the bone — continues over a period of three to six months or longer, depending on individual factors. Your dental team will schedule follow-up appointments to monitor progress at each stage.

mainEntity.name: Can primary closure fail after dental implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: In some cases, the gum tissue may separate slightly after surgery — a situation called wound dehiscence. This does not automatically mean the implant will fail. Many factors influence whether minor wound breakdown affects the long-term outcome, including the extent of separation, how quickly it is identified, and how the area is managed. If you notice any changes to the wound site, contact your dental team for assessment and guidance.

mainEntity.name: Is primary closure always possible with dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Primary closure is always the surgical goal, but it is not achievable in every case. Factors such as the volume of available gum tissue, the complexity of bone grafting, the number of implants being placed, and the anatomy of the surgical site can all affect what is achievable. Your dental surgeon will plan your treatment with closure in mind and will explain what to expect based on your individual circumstances.

mainEntity.name: Why does smoking affect primary closure and implant healing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Smoking impairs the body's healing response in several ways. It reduces blood flow to the surgical site, decreases the effectiveness of the immune system in fighting infection, and slows the cellular processes involved in tissue repair. These effects can compromise primary closure and increase the risk of complications including wound breakdown, infection, and implant failure. Patients are strongly advised to avoid smoking before and after implant surgery.

mainEntity.name: What should I eat to support healing after implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the days immediately following surgery, a soft diet is recommended. Suitable foods include yoghurt, mashed vegetables, scrambled eggs, soft fish, and soup (not too hot). Hard, crunchy, chewy, or very hot foods should be avoided, as they can place pressure on the healing site or disrupt the sutures and blood clot. Your dental team will advise when it is safe to reintroduce a more varied diet based on your healing progress.

mainEntity.name: When should I be concerned about my implant healing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mild discomfort, swelling, and bruising are expected in the first few days following implant surgery and are a normal part of the healing response. However, you should consider contacting your dental team if pain is worsening rather than improving after 72 hours, if swelling is increasing rather than reducing, if you notice signs of possible infection such as discharge or a persistent unpleasant taste, or if the wound appears to be opening. Your dental team is best placed to assess whether any follow-up is needed.
